review.name: Code Review
review.description: One agent reads and explains the code, the other hunts for bugs and improvements.

roles.focus: Read the code thoroughly and describe what it does, how it works, and document its behavior. Provide a clear summary of the architecture, data flow, and key decisions.
Analyze the code for bugs, security issues, performance problems, and improvement opportunities. Challenge assumptions and suggest concrete fixes with code examples.

implement.name: Implementation
implement.description: Lead plans architecture and task breakdown, worker writes code and tests.

roles.focus: Plan the architecture, break down the task into clear steps, define interfaces and contracts. Review the worker's code for correctness and design alignment. Share your plan before any coding starts.
Write the implementation code and tests based on the architect's plan. Report progress after each step, surface blockers quickly, and ensure all tests pass before marking complete.

research.name: Research
research.description: Both agents independently research the topic and then compare findings.

roles.focus: Independently research the topic from a technical/implementation angle. Focus on how things work, existing solutions, code examples, and technical trade-offs. Share your findings for comparison.

Independently research the topic from an ecosystem/alternatives angle. Focus on available tools, libraries, best practices, community patterns, and real-world usage. Share your findings for comparison.

debug.name: Debug
debug.description: One agent reproduces the bug, the other analyzes root cause.

roles.focus: Reproduce the bug reliably. Create a minimal reproduction case, document exact steps to trigger it, capture error messages and stack traces. Share reproduction steps with your teammate.
Analyze the root cause of the bug. Read relevant code paths, trace the execution flow, identify where the logic breaks down. Propose and implement a fix once the reproducer confirms the bug.

adversarial.name: Adversarial Review
adversarial.description: One agent implements, the other tries to break it with edge case tests.

roles.focus: Implement the requested change. Write clean, correct code. After the adversary finds issues, fix them and explain your fix. Your goal: code that survives all attacks.

Your ONLY job is to find bugs, edge cases, and failures. Write tests that break the builder's code. Check race conditions, boundary values, error handling, security. Never approve until you've tried at least 10 attack vectors. Be ruthless.

crypto-strategy.name: Crypto Strategy Development
crypto-strategy.description: One agent designs strategy logic, the other backtests and validates edge.

roles.focus: Design the strategy: entry/exit logic, indicators, parameters. Read existing strategies in scripts/paper/strategies/ for patterns. Define clear hypothesis and expected edge. Share design before implementation.

Backtest the quant's strategy. Run scripts/backtest/test_correctness.py. Check for overfitting, survivorship bias, fee assumptions. Challenge every assumption. Only approve if Sharpe > 1.0 and profit factor > 1.2 on out-of-sample data.

deep-research.name: Deep Research with Convergence
deep-research.description: Two agents research independently then cross-validate. High-confidence findings = both agree.

roles.focus: Research from primary sources: documentation, code, APIs, databases. Focus on FACTS and DATA. Share numbered findings. After comparing with secondary researcher, rate each finding: CONFIRMED (both found it), UNIQUE (only you found it), CONTRADICTED (disagreement).

Research from secondary sources: papers, forums, community, real-world examples. Focus on CONTEXT and PATTERNS. Share numbered findings. After comparing with primary researcher, challenge any finding that lacks evidence. Only CONFIRMED findings go into final report.

ultrareview.name: Ultra Review (4-Agent Security Pass)
ultrareview.description: Four-agent deep review: auditor reads, adversary attacks, validator checks empirically, synthesizer signs off.

roles.focus: Walk the entire change set, identify risk surface, document behaviour changes, and flag anything outside the stated scope. Produce a numbered findings list ordered by severity.
Attack the change: craft inputs that break invariants, probe for auth/injection/race bugs, challenge every assumption. Never sign off until you've exhausted at least 10 attack vectors.
Run the tests, the linters, the type-checker, and any verify scripts that apply. Report empirical results with command lines and exit codes. No claim without evidence.
Consolidate findings from the other three, resolve contradictions, and give an explicit GO / NO-GO verdict with justification. Never green-light unresolved HIGH severity items.

premium-quad.name: Premium Quad (Critical / Live-Deploy)
premium-quad.description: Four-agent critical-work pipeline: architect designs, implementer executes, adversary attacks, reviewer gates.

roles.focus: Design the change with production constraints front of mind: blast radius, rollback, observability. Share the plan and get explicit agreement before implementation begins.
Execute the architect's plan pragmatically: clean diffs, matching tests, incremental commits. Surface any design deviation before writing code that depends on it.
Break what the implementer just built: race conditions, partial-failure modes, migration edge cases. Then help patch the holes you exposed.
Independent final gate. Read the complete diff with fresh eyes, demand evidence for risky claims, and give an explicit YES / NO verdict with one-line justification.

audit-only.name: Audit Only (Read-Only Sweep)
audit-only.description: Three agents read and analyze without editing. Output is a structured fix-list the operator implements manually. Use when scope is large, primitives are at risk, or recovery from a bad write would be expensive.

roles.focus: READ-ONLY MODE — no file edits, no commits, no mutating shell commands. Map the surface area: enumerate files in scope, group by concern, surface dependencies between them. Identify pain points and risks WITHOUT proposing concrete patches yet. Output: structured inventory (file, role, LOC, observed issues) for the analysts to dig into.

READ-ONLY MODE — no file edits, no commits, no mutating commands. For each item the MAPPER inventories, dig into the code and produce concrete observations: what's wrong, why it matters, what minimal change would fix it (file:line + before/after sketch — but DO NOT apply the change). Cite evidence. Group findings by severity (CRIT / HIGH / MED / LOW).

READ-ONLY MODE — no file edits, no commits, no mutating commands. Consolidate MAPPER's inventory + ANALYST's findings into a deliverable fix-list the operator can hand off to a manual implementation pass. Format: numbered action items with file:line, severity, suggested fix sketch, and estimated edit scope. Reject any item that lacks a concrete fix sketch — the goal is actionable, not philosophical. Save the doc as docs/AUDIT_<topic>.md before team-done.

pentest.name: Penetration Test (Authorized Targets Only)
pentest.description: Three-agent RECON → EXPLOIT → VERIFY pipeline for authorized security testing of systems you own or have written permission to test. Non-destructive proofs only.

roles.focus: AUTHORIZATION GATE FIRST: confirm the target is owned by the user or has explicit written test authorization. If unclear, STOP and ask. Then map the attack surface — endpoints, auth flows, version fingerprints, exposed config, third-party deps, file-upload paths, error messages that leak. NO exploits in this phase, only enumeration. Output: scoped attack plan with prioritized targets ranked by likely impact and exploit feasibility. Note any out-of-scope assets discovered (mark, do not test).

Test prioritized vulnerabilities from RECON's plan against in-scope targets only. Cover OWASP Top 10 (SQLi, XSS, IDOR, broken access control, auth bypass, SSRF, deserialization, security misconfiguration, vulnerable deps), business-logic flaws, and race conditions. Each finding must include: minimal reproducible PoC, affected endpoint(s) with parameter, observed behavior vs. expected. NEVER destructive — no DROP/DELETE/rm payloads, no mass requests, no credential brute-force on real user accounts, no DoS testing. Stop at proof. If you find auth bypass or RCE, demonstrate with whoami/SELECT 1 — never escalate further. Out-of-scope hits get logged for RECON to verify, not exploited.

Validate every EXPLOITER finding in a clean environment — re-run the PoC, confirm reproduction, reject false positives explicitly. Score severity using CVSS v3 with environmental adjustment for this system's actual deployment (auth model, data sensitivity, exposure). For each confirmed finding: write a one-line root cause, the surgical fix (line refs / sanitizer / header / ACL change), the verification command the defender runs to confirm the fix worked, and a regression test recommendation. Output is a prioritized findings document the user can hand to a developer. Never sign off on Critical/High without a fix recommendation. List `targets_tested` and `out_of_scope_skipped` in the final report so scope is auditable.

thinking.name: Thinking Mode (structured hypothesis → evidence → decision)
thinking.description: Force the team into a deliberate reasoning protocol: frame the problem with hypotheses, gather evidence for each, challenge before deciding, then act and verify. Supervisor catches unverified claims and circling. Use when correctness matters more than speed.

roles.focus: Own the investigation. Frame the problem, enumerate 2-5 hypotheses (team-think hypothesize), gather evidence for each (team-think evidence). Do NOT pick a decision alone — wait for the challenger's critique before team-think decide. Reflect on what you learned before team-done.

Own the critique. Actively challenge every hypothesis the investigator proposes (team-think challenge). Demand evidence. Propose competing hypotheses. Only agree to a decision after the evidence is strong enough that you would bet on it. Your job is to prevent groupthink, not to agree.
